newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish shares close at new high led by banks.
newsitem.headline: Swedish shares close at new high led by banks.

text.p: Swedish shares closed at a new record high on Thursday, boosted by gains in New York and with rumours fuelling the banking sector which outperformed the rest of the market.
The Stockholm general index closed 1.57 percent higher at 3,276.79 in fairly hefty turnover of 6.04 billion crowns.
"The market is rather optimistic at the moment with a lot of bargain hunting in the small medium capitalised companies that have been laggging the index," said one broker.
"I think we will see this trend continuing."
But a key focus of the day was banks amid market rumours.

The banking sector rose 4.79 percent, aided by a stronger debt market and dollar strength, but mainly due to some kind of bank warrant issued by a large foreign player in the market and renewed talk about restructuring of the financial sector.
Handelsbanken gained 17 crowns to 250 while S-E-Banken rose six to 96.50 and Nordbanken climbed 10 to 277 crowns.
"There are a lot of rumours again about a merger of S-E-Banken and Handelsbanken," said one broker, adding that Nordbanken could be involved too.
The building and construction sector also performed well, with the index rising 2.76 percent. A broker said interest in the sector was picking up rapidly with interest rates still low.
Investment group Investor rose two crowns to 427 after posting a 69 percent total return in the 12 months to June 30, 1997 against the sharemarket's 56 percent.
Lock maker Assa Abloy closed three higher at 181 crowns after posting a 51 percent rise in first half profit after financial items to 225 million crowns.
Drugs major Astra rose 0.5 crowns to 152.5 ahead of posting its six months results on Friday.
The other market heavyweight, telecoms giant Ericsson, closed 2.5 up at 371.5 crowns.
